moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how a codeless test is created in Testim by recording actions in the AUT browser.
Explain weighted element identification and the limits of Smart Locator resilience.
Explain how a recorded test is saved and how its results are viewed after a run.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Creating a basic test by recording

elements.description: Creating a test starts by navigating to the relevant website inside the Application Under Test (AUT) browser window and recording the series of actions you want tested — clicks, text entry, scrolling, navigation. Testim captures each action as a step.
Recorded actions appear as individual steps with action-type icons. Execution follows the configured sequence; edit the test as needed rather than assuming the original recording order is permanent.

elements.text: The basic recording workflow needs no user-written script. Add outcome validations and edit supported step properties or sequence when the test requires them.

bulletPoints: Record actions in the AUT browser → each action becomes an editable step.
Codeless: no code needed to get a first working test from a recording.

elements.description: Testim identifies targets using many weighted attributes and can improve identification across runs. Other useful attributes may preserve a match after a change, but resilience does not guarantee success or the correct target in every changed UI.

elements.text: Inspect the actual target and asserted outcome after UI changes. Improve updates identification of the existing target; Reassign selects a different target and replaces its locators. Neither replaces business-result validations.

bulletPoints: Weighted attributes help identify elements and adapt to changes.
Validate target correctness; locator resilience is not a guarantee.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Saving a test and viewing results

elements.description: Save the named test in the project library. Editor, CLI and scheduling provide different execution paths; available configuration and permissions still govern a run.

Inspect executed-step statuses and available error details, including expected and actual validation values. Failure evidence supports diagnosis but is not a guarantee that the root cause is already identified.

bulletPoints: Save the test and choose an appropriate execution path.
Review step statuses and error evidence to investigate a failed run.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming 'codeless' means 'unchangeable'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a recorded test as a fixed artifact that must be re-recorded from scratch whenever it needs a change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Edit supported step properties and targets, add validations or change sequence as needed; a small change need not require a new whole recording.

examPitfalls.title: Treating locator resilience as guaranteed correctness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every changed UI will still pass with the correct target.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check target identification and outcome assertions. Improve refreshes the existing target; Reassign selects a different one. Inspect failures rather than automatically trusting or replacing every locator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented basic recording workflow, how is a codeless test created?

options.text: By writing Selenium scripts behind the scenes that the user must review.
By recording the series of actions taken in the AUT browser and turning each into an editable step.
By importing a manual test case document and converting it automatically.
By requiring the user to describe the test in plain English to an AI chatbot.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Creating a test starts with recording the actions taken in the AUT browser; each action becomes a step in the test procedure. No manual scripting, document import, or chatbot description is required for this basic flow.

optionExplanations.A: The basic workflow does not require users to review Selenium scripts.
optionExplanations.B: Recording AUT actions produces editable steps.
optionExplanations.C: Automatic manual-document conversion is not this recording workflow.
optionExplanations.D: A chatbot description is not required for basic recording.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the main purpose of Testim's Smart Locators?

options.text: To speed up test recording by skipping element analysis entirely.
To identify a target using weighted attributes and help maintain identification as attributes change.
To automatically translate the test into another programming language.
To generate documentation for every step in the test.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about resilience to change, not speed or translation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Weighted attributes support resilient element identification. Changing attributes may still leave useful matching evidence; this does not guarantee every changed UI succeeds or that outcome assertions are unnecessary.

optionExplanations.A: Element analysis is central to weighted identification.
optionExplanations.B: Weighted attributes support target identification without guaranteeing every changed UI succeeds.
optionExplanations.C: Locators identify elements rather than translate programming languages.
optionExplanations.D: Their purpose is identification, not step documentation generation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does each box in the recorded test procedure represent?

options.text: A step, with an icon indicating the type of action performed.
A folder in the Test Library.
A user account used during the recording.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each box maps 1:1 to a recorded action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each box represents a step in the test procedure, with an icon in the upper-left corner indicating the type of action (click, enter text, scroll, etc.). It is not a separate test, a folder, or a user account.

optionExplanations.A: A step belongs to a test; it is not itself a separate test case.
optionExplanations.B: The box represents a step and its icon identifies the action type.
optionExplanations.C: A procedure step is not a library folder.
optionExplanations.D: The icon describes an action, not the recording user account.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After running a saved test, what does Testim surface to help you diagnose a failure?

options.text: Only a generic pass/fail flag for the entire test, with no further detail.
The per-step pass/fail result along with the reason a step failed.
A full video of a human manually re-running the test.
Nothing — results must be inspected by re-running the test manually.

practiceQuiz.hint: Diagnosis works at the step level, not just the whole-test level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Executed-step status and available failure details support investigation. A validation error may include expected and actual values; those details are evidence, not a guaranteed complete root-cause analysis.

optionExplanations.A: Available step detail goes beyond a whole-test flag.
optionExplanations.B: Step status and failure evidence help diagnose the run.
optionExplanations.C: A human manual replay video is not the documented failure-detail mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: Results provide evidence without requiring a manual replay for every failure.

quickRecap.value: Recording produces editable action steps without user-written scripting.
Weighted attributes can improve identification resilience; verify the target and outcome.
Save tests in the project library and select a supported execution path.
Inspect executed-step statuses and available error evidence; diagnose the actual cause.
